proof_quality.rationale: The proof summary demonstrates exhaustive search across multiple repositories: Guerrero civil registration (seven attempts, documented search gaps), Catholic baptism records (indexed portion searched, unindexed volumes explained), and 1930 Mexico National Census. Three independent sources converge: (1) 1910 civil birth registration naming Sóstenes Cruz as father; (2) 1935 marriage registration of sibling Primitivo Corona independently naming both parents; (3) 1930 census showing Apolinar Corona (widowed) enumerated with all known siblings. The narrative addresses the birth-year discrepancy (1910 civil vs. 1914 census) with sound reasoning about census approximation artifacts. The declared tier 'proved' matches the evidence: two independent original civil records from different informants, 25 years apart, with structural census corroboration, and no contradicting evidence. All five GPS components explicitly claimed as met. The proof is comprehensive, well-reasoned, and proportionate to the tier.

entry.question: Who were the parents of Mauro Cruz Corona, born about 1910 in or near Nueva Italia, Michoacán, Mexico?
entry.rationale: This is the central stated objective. Civil registration in Michoacán was established by 1859; records for ca. 1910 likely survive at the registro civil for the Apatzingán / Nueva Italia area. A civil birth record (acta de nacimiento) would directly name both parents. The subject's siblings in the tree (Miguel, Liborio, Facundo Cruz) share the Cruz paternal surname, consistent with the father carrying the surname Cruz; 'Corona' in Mauro's compound surname likely represents the maternal line. Answering this question depends on first locating the exact birth record, which is also the vehicle for the birth-date/place question.

# Locality Guide: Nueva Italia de Ruiz (Apatzingán Municipality), Michoacán, Mexico (1890–1930)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Specific place:** Nueva Italia de Ruiz — a city established ca. 1909 as an agricultural colony in the Tierra Caliente lowlands; FamilySearch standardPlace: *Nueva Italia de Ruiz, Múgica, Michoacan, Mexico*
- **1890–1951 administrative jurisdiction:** Municipality of **Apatzingán**, within the Tepalcatepec region of Michoacán. The municipality of Múgica did not exist until 1951, when it was carved from Apatzingán. All civil and church records from ca. 1910 will be filed under **Apatzingán municipality**.
- **County seat (Apatzingán municipality):** Apatzingán de la Constitución (city, est. 1617/+)
- **Parent state:** Michoacán — admitted to Mexico 22 December 1823
- **Economy:** Agricultural region (Tierra Caliente lowlands — cotton, sesame, cattle ranching); Nueva Italia was a planned agricultural colony.
- **Religious denomination:** Predominantly Roman Catholic; Archdiocese of Morelia. Main parish: Nuestra Señora de la Asunción, Apatzingán.
- **Language of records:** Spanish.
- **Key historical events:** Mexican Revolution (1910–1920); Cristero War (1926–1929) — both may have disrupted civil and church record-keeping.

## Boundary changes
- Before 1951: Nueva Italia de Ruiz was part of Apatzingán municipality. Civil registration records from 1890–1930 are filed under Apatzingán at the Registro Civil de Apatzingán.
- 1951: Múgica municipality created from Apatzingán territory; subsequent records under Múgica.
- FamilySearch implication: When browsing collection 1916243, select Apatzingán as the municipality.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- Civil registration began in Michoacán at the municipal level in 1859; compliance not strict until 1867.
- FamilySearch collection 1916243 (Mexico, Michoacán, Civil Registration, 1859–1940): indexed + images; browse by municipality.
- Birth records name: date/place, child's name/gender, parents' names/ages/civil status, paternal grandparents, maternal grandparents.
- Apatzingán birth (Nacimientos) volumes confirmed: 1898–1905 and 1912–1921 (100% indexed); 1906–1911 not confirmed in first page of results — verify in collection browser.
- Ancestry collection 60415 (Civil Registration Births, 1859–1934): index + images ($).

### Church records
- Primary parish: Nuestra Señora de la Asunción, Apatzingán (Archdiocese of Morelia)
- FamilySearch: Baptisms 1896–1899 (004087244) — indexed + full-text searchable; Matrimonios parroquiales 1894–1909 (004737147) — full-text searchable, browse-only images; Información matrimonial 1866–1920 — browse-only images (0% indexed).
- FamilySearch collection 1883388 (Catholic Church Records 1555–1996): index only.
- Ancestry collection 60021 (Michoacán Catholic Church Records 1649–1909): images ($).

### Census records
- 1930 Mexico National Census: FamilySearch collection 1307314 — indexed + images; Ancestry collection 1771 ($).
- Apatzingán-specific 1930 census volumes: 44–76% indexed on FamilySearch.

### Immigration / border crossing records
- FamilySearch collection 1803932 (US Border Crossings 1903–1957): indexed.
- Ancestry collection 1082 (Border Crossings 1895–1964): indexed + images ($).

## Research tips
1. Search Apatzingán, not Múgica or Nueva Italia, for 1910-era records in FamilySearch collection 1916243.
2. Decode the compound surname: Cruz = paternal, Corona = maternal.
3. Birth records name grandparents — useful for two-generation extension.
4. Search siblings' birth records (Miguel, Liborio, Facundo Cruz) to confirm parents' names.
5. Supplement civil with Catholic records (Nuestra Señora de la Asunción, Apatzingán) when civil records are missing.
6. Women keep maiden surnames in all Mexican records.
7. 190 FamilySearch volumes match Apatzingán 1890–1930; only 50 examined — browse the full collection for gap years.

entry.rationale: The civil birth register (nacimiento) for Mauro Cruz Corona is the highest-probability direct evidence for his parentage. FamilySearch collection 1916243 (Mexico, Michoacán, Civil Registration, 1859-1940) covers Apatzingán municipality indexed + images. Per loc_001: in 1910, Nueva Italia de Ruiz was administratively part of Apatzingán municipality — the registro civil filed births under Apatzingán. Birth records in this collection name: child's name/gender, date/place of birth, parents' names/ages/civil status, paternal grandparents, and maternal grandparents — directly answering the parentage question. Search by child's given name 'Mauro' and paternal surname 'Cruz' in the Apatzingán municipality section of collection 1916243. Also try variants (Mauro/Mauro de Cruz) and year range 1907-1914 given 'about 1910' estimate.

Mauro's known siblings — Miguel Cruz, Liborio Cruz, and Facundo Cruz — were born in the same family and registered in the same Apatzingán civil registry. Their nacimiento records would independently name Mauro's parents, corroborating item 1 and providing FAN evidence bearing directly on the question's subject. This is the mandatory FAN item for this parentage question (BCG Standard 14). The wider date range (1895-1920) accounts for uncertainty in sibling birth years. Search FamilySearch collection 1916243 for each sibling name in Apatzingán births. All three sibling names share the Cruz paternal surname and should yield entries naming the father (Cruz) and mother (Corona); their records also list grandparents, extending the pedigree. Note: the siblings in the tree currently lack maternal surnames — their nacimientos would supply those, confirming the Corona maternal line.

A dedicated search for the civil marriage record between Mauro's father (surname Cruz) and his mother (surname Corona) in Apatzingán, per the parentage-question requirement in references/record-type-guide.md. The marriage record: (a) confirms the couple as a unit; (b) supplies the mother's full name — including her exact given name and any maternal surname beyond 'Corona'; (c) by its date relative to ca. 1910 birth, corroborates a father otherwise named only in Mauro's birth record. Search FamilySearch collection 1916243, Apatzingán Matrimonios, for groom surnamed Cruz marrying a woman surnamed Corona. Per loc_001, Apatzingán civil Matrimonios volumes for 1895-1930 are confirmed 100% indexed. Date range 1885-1910 is sized to cover plausible marriage years for parents of a child born ca. 1910 (parents likely born ca. 1860-1890). NOTE: the couple's marriage proves their union and its date but does not, by itself, prove Mauro is their child — that link requires the child's own birth/baptism record (item 1).

Full-text co-occurrence search for the paternal surname 'Cruz' + maternal surname 'Corona' across Michoacán civil registration records. Per loc_001, the confirmed indexed Nacimientos volumes for Apatzingán do not include 1906-1911 in the first scan of results (190 total volumes; only 50 examined). A full-text search using both surnames as required co-occurrence terms will surface any birth or family entry in those gap years that is not name-indexed. Per references/record-type-guide.md: for a compound Iberian surname 'Given Paterno Materno', the co-occurrence '+Cruz +Corona' will find acts where both surnames appear together — the child's baptism, a parent's burial, or their marriage. Execute via the search-full-text skill against the statewide Michoacán civil registration corpus. This is fallback for item 1 when the indexed name search misses the record.

Catholic baptism record for Mauro Cruz Corona at Nuestra Señora de la Asunción, Apatzingán — the primary parish for this area per loc_001. A baptism record names the parents (father and mother) and godparents (padrinos), who were frequently relatives or neighbors and provide FAN context. FamilySearch collection 1883388 (Mexico, Michoacan, Catholic Church Records, 1555-1996) offers an index. Baptism volumes for Nuestra Señora de la Asunción are confirmed on FamilySearch: 1896-1899 (image group 004087244, ~98% indexed + full-text); the ca. 1910 volumes may be browse-only image groups under 004730413 (libro 7 covers 1919-1920 combined; earlier baptism volumes for 1905-1918 may require catalog search). Also check Ancestry collection 60021 (Michoacán Catholic Church Records 1649-1909) for the pre-1910 portion. Parish records are in Spanish and may use the narrative handwriting style.

entry.rationale: Mauro Cruz Corona, born ca. 1910, would appear approximately age 20 in the 1930 Mexico National Census. FamilySearch collection 1307314 is indexed + images; Apatzingán-specific 1930 volumes are 44-76% indexed per loc_001. If Mauro appears in a household headed by a Cruz family member, the head's relationship to other members may identify his parents. Co-residents or neighboring households named Cruz or Corona in the Apatzingán / Nueva Italia area also provide FAN context and may help identify which Cruz or Corona family is the correct one. Even a finding of Mauro living independently narrows the search by confirming his age and residence.

Ancestry collection 60415 (Michoacan, Mexico, Civil Registration Births, 1859-1934) provides index + images for Michoacán civil birth records, potentially with different indexing coverage or transcription than FamilySearch collection 1916243. If Mauro's nacimiento is not found in items 1 or 4, Ancestry's version may index the same Apatzingán registers differently, catch variant spellings of 'Mauro' or 'Cruz', or offer a supplementary image pathway. Subscription required; also accessible for free at FamilySearch Centers and affiliated libraries. This is the paid fallback for item 1.

exhaustive_declaration.justification: Three of the seven stop criteria fail: repository_breadth (siblings' nacimientos, parents' marriage record, Catholic baptism, and 1930 census in Guerrero are all unsearched — pli_002, pli_003, pli_005, pli_006, and pli_007 are all in 'planned' status), independent_verification (only one source, one informant unit — the father at civil registration; no independent corroboration exists), and overturn_risk (a single unsearched sibling nacimiento in Guerrero could independently confirm or contradict the parentage and resolve the transcription ambiguity in the mother's surname). Hard precondition also not met: pli_001 status is 'in_progress' (factual work complete but status not updated), and pli_002–pli_007 are all 'planned'. The plan must be redirected to Guerrero (La Unión de Isidoro Montes de Oca / Coahuayutla municipalities, collection 1918291) and remaining items executed before exhaustiveness can be declared.

stop_criteria.goal_alignment: Partially met. The civil birth registration ark:/61903/1:1:QGWQ-MCFV names Sóstenes Cruz as father and Apolinar Corona as mother, with the father personally present and acting as informant — a convincing answer is available from this one record. The geographic assumption of Nueva Italia, Michoacán was corrected to La Unión de Isidoro Montes de Oca, Guerrero, which is consistent with all three known siblings also being born in Guerrero. The parentage answer is available but rests on a single source; broader confirmation is needed before the goal is fully and independently established.
stop_criteria.repository_breadth: FAILS. Only one search yielded a result (pli_001, Michoacán broadened to all Mexico). FAN research required by BCG Standard 14 — siblings' nacimientos in Guerrero (pli_002) — has not been attempted. The parents' civil marriage record in Guerrero (pli_003) has not been searched. The Catholic baptism in the relevant Guerrero parish (pli_005) has not been searched. The 1930 Mexico National Census for Mauro (pli_006) has not been searched. The Ancestry fallback for Guerrero (pli_007) has not been attempted. All five remaining plan items target Guerrero (collection 1918291) rather than Michoacán as originally planned. The jurisdiction correction from Michoacán to Guerrero makes all five items newly relevant unsearched avenues.
stop_criteria.original_substitution: Met for the one source in hand. The civil birth registration (ark:/61903/1:1:QGWQ-MCFV) is an original civil registration image from collection 1918291 (Mexico, Guerrero, Civil Registration, 1860–1996); it was accessed as an image, not via a derivative index alone. No derivative-only sources are cited.
stop_criteria.independent_verification: FAILS. Only one source exists — the civil birth registration — and all parentage assertions (a_008 for Sóstenes Cruz as father, a_011 for Apolinar Corona as mother) derive from a single informant unit: the father Sóstenes Cruz, who appeared at the registry. The siblings' nacimientos, the parents' marriage record, and the Catholic baptism would each constitute independent sources with different informants and institutional origins. None has been searched. Two sources from different informants are required; only one informant unit is currently on record.
stop_criteria.evidence_class: Met. The civil birth registration is an original record (created at the time of the event by a civil registrar with witnesses) and carries primary information for parentage (the father was present and stated the facts from personal knowledge, per informant_proximity: self / household_member on the parentage assertions). This criterion is satisfied by the single record in hand.
stop_criteria.conflict_resolution: Met. No conflicts are registered in the project. The discrepancy between the question's assumption of Michoacán origin and the record's Guerrero birthplace is explained by the evidence itself (family migrated from Guerrero to Nueva Italia, Michoacán; all three known siblings are also recorded as born in Guerrero) and does not constitute an unresolved conflict. The transcription ambiguity in the mother's surname ('Co??na' vs. 'Corona') was resolved by corrected standard reading of the original image and is documented in informant_bias_notes on a_009; it is not an outstanding conflict. No competing assertions name different parents.
stop_criteria.overturn_risk: FAILS. Risk is elevated. With only one record and no independent verification, the following unsearched sources could plausibly alter or complicate the conclusion: (1) Siblings' nacimientos in Guerrero (pli_002) would independently name the parents — if a sibling's record names different parents or an unexpected maternal surname for 'Corona', the conclusion would require revision; (2) The parents' civil marriage record (pli_003) would confirm the Cruz–Corona union and the mother's full name — if no such marriage record exists or names a different woman, that is significant; (3) The Catholic baptism in Guerrero (pli_005) would provide an independent religious-record confirmation with its own informant chain. Civil registration in Guerrero began by 1860 per the Mexico Civil Registration wiki (FamilySearch, https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Mexico_Civil_Registration), well before Mauro's 1910 birth; the baptism is therefore corroborating rather than the primary gating record. The transcription ambiguity in 'Apolinar Co??na' — resolved in this record but unconfirmed independently — is a specific overturn-risk vector that a sibling's record would close.

entry.guide_markdown:
# Locality Guide: La Unión de Isidoro Montes de Oca, Guerrero, Mexico (1890–1930)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** Municipality established ca. 1849; Montes de Oca judicial district formed ca. 1898
- **County seat / administrative center:** La Unión de Isidoro Montes de Oca
- **Parent jurisdiction:** State of Guerrero, Mexico
- **Economy:** Agriculture, fishing, coastal lowlands; haciendas and small farms
- **Ethnic composition:** Mestizo majority; Nahua and Mixtec communities in surrounding area
- **Religious denominations:** Roman Catholic — parish of San Felipe de Jesús, La Unión; diocese of Chilapa (later Chilpancingo-Chilapa)
- **Key historical events:** Mexican Revolution (1910–1920) disrupted civil registration in parts of Guerrero

## Boundary changes
- La Unión is stable as a municipality across the 1890–1930 period.
- **Critical archiving exception:** Guerrero civil records are recorded at the municipio level but **archived at the judicial district level** (Montes de Oca district). Per the FamilySearch Wiki: "The exceptions are the states of Guerrero and Oaxaca, where the records are recorded by the municipio but are archived on a district level." ([Mexico Civil Registration](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Mexico_Civil_Registration))

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date:** Civil registration began in Guerrero in 1860 at the municipio level; archived under Montes de Oca judicial district
- **What exists:** Births (nacimientos), marriages (matrimonios), deaths (defunciones), 1860–1996
- **Where held:** FamilySearch collection **1918291** ("México, Guerrero, Registro Civil, 1860–1996"); 1.73 million records; indexed + images online. Filter to "La Unión" or "Montes de Oca" within the collection.
- **Gaps:** Revolution period ca. 1913–1920 may have reduced registration completeness
- **Access level:** Indexed + images (most civil registration volumes)

### Church records
- **Denominations present:** Roman Catholic — San Felipe de Jesús parish
- **Record types:** Baptisms, marriages, burials, confirmations
- **Where held:** FamilySearch collection **1823323** ("Mexico, Guerrero, Catholic Church Records, 1576–1979"); 2.58 million records
  - **Baptisms** (San Felipe de Jesús, La Unión, 1890–1930): ~20 volumes; **77–97% name-indexed**, full-text searchable — indexed + images
  - **Confirmations** (La Unión, 1902–1920): 2 volumes; **0% name-indexed**, full-text searchable — full-text only
  - **Marriages** (La Unión, 1878–1930): ~5 volumes; **0% name-indexed**, full-text searchable — full-text only; browse-only fallback
- **Language:** Spanish

### Census records
- **National census (1930):** Mexico National Census, 1930 — La Unión image groups (DGS 004107152, 004107154); **48–69% name-indexed**, **NOT full-text searchable** — missing entries require page-by-page browsing
- **Earlier censuses (1895, 1900, 1910):** Limited digitization for Guerrero; check FamilySearch for available volumes
- **Access:** 1930 partially indexed; unindexed portions browse-only

### Probate and court records
- **Types:** Testamentos, intestados, guardianships — filed at Juzgado de Primera Instancia, Montes de Oca district
- **Where held:** Archivo General del Estado de Guerrero (AGEG), Chilpancingo — physical only
- **Access:** Physical only; no FamilySearch digitization found

### Land records
- **Survey system:** Metes and bounds; colonial-era grants; post-1917 ejido records
- **Where held:** AGN (federal grants); AGEG (state/local)
- **Access:** Physical or AGN online portal; limited FamilySearch coverage

### Military records
- **Relevant conflicts:** Mexican Revolution (1910–1920)
- **Where held:** AHSDN (Mexico City); AGN
- **Access:** Physical or mail inquiry

### Cemetery records
- **Major cemeteries:** Municipal cemetery La Unión; San Felipe de Jesús church cemetery
- **Online coverage:** FindAGrave/BillionGraves coverage sparse for this region

### Newspaper records
- **Local papers:** Limited local press for rural Guerrero 1890–1930; state papers in Chilpancingo
- **Where held:** Hemeroteca Nacional Digital de México (hndm.unam.mx)

### Immigration/emigration records
- **Note:** Cruz-Corona family undertook internal migration (Guerrero → Michoacán) — not international
- **For US border crossings if any:** NARA border crossing manifests; FamilySearch indexed

### Tax records
- **Types:** Padrones fiscales, contribución directa
- **Where held:** AGEG; limited digitization

### Other record types
- **Notarial records:** Contracts, wills, sales — Archivo Notarial del Estado de Guerrero or AGEG
- **School records:** Registros de inscripción — held locally or at state archives

## Repository guide

### Online repositories
| Repository | Collections for this place | Access |
|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | Catholic Church Records 1576–1979 (col. 1823323, 2.58M); Civil Registration 1860–1996 (col. 1918291, 1.73M); 1930 Mexico Census image groups (DGS 004107152, 004107154) | Free |
| Ancestry | Mexico vital records via Ancestry partnership | Subscription |

**Coverage of this survey:** 39 digitized volumes match La Unión de Isidoro Montes de Oca for 1890–1930; the categories above represent the complete returned set for this period.

### Physical repositories
| Repository | Holdings | Access method |
|---|---|---|
| AGEG, Chilpancingo | State civil records, court/probate, land records | In-person or mail |
| Registro Civil de La Unión | Local civil registration originals | In-person |
| AGN, Mexico City | Federal land, immigration, military records | In-person or online |
| Diocesan Archive, Chilpancingo-Chilapa | Parish register backups, confirmations | Contact diocese |
| Parish of San Felipe de Jesús, La Unión | Original parish registers | Contact parish |

## Records NOT online
- Guerrero probate/court records (Montes de Oca district): physical at AGEG
- Land records: physical at AGEG or AGN
- Military records (Revolution-era): physical at AHSDN
- Pre-1860 church records not yet microfilmed

## Known record losses
- Mexican Revolution (1910–1920): disrupted civil registration in parts of Guerrero; nacimiento and matrimonio volumes from ca. 1913–1920 may be incomplete.

## Research tips
- **Guerrero civil records use district-level archiving** — search under Montes de Oca district per [Mexico Civil Registration](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Mexico_Civil_Registration)
- **Catholic marriages are 0% name-indexed** — use full-text search for Cruz and Corona surnames
- **1930 census is 48–69% indexed and NOT full-text searchable** — unindexed entries require page-by-page browsing of DGS 004107152/004107154
- **Compound surnames**: Cruz = paternal surname (Sóstenes Cruz); Corona = maternal surname (Apolinar Corona)
- **Sibling birth records** for Miguel Cruz (1913), Liborio Cruz (1916), Facundo Cruz (1918) are in collection 1918291 and corroborate parental identities
- Consult Mexico-level wiki pages: [Mexico Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Mexico_Genealogy), [Mexico Online Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Mexico_Online_Genealogy_Records), [Mexico Research Tips](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Mexico_Research_Tips_and_Strategies)

The underlying image (ark:/61903/3:1:33S7-9T8R-68V) must be read to confirm whether the surname is 'Corona' as asserted in a_008/a_009. Until the image confirms the transcription, 'Corona' rests on a partial index read; all subsequent Cruz×Corona searches depend on this validation. This is the quickest verification step: read the specific image page and transcribe the handwritten surname.

entry.jurisdiction: La Unión de Isidoro Montes de Oca, Guerrero, Mexico (Montes de Oca judicial district); Coahuayutla de José María Izazaga, Guerrero, Mexico
entry.rationale: Three known siblings were born in Guerrero: Miguel Cruz (b. ca. 24 Apr 1913, El Coco, La Unión, Guerrero), Liborio Cruz (b. ca. 23 Jul 1916, Pochutla, Coahuayutla, Guerrero), and Facundo Cruz (b. ca. 27 Nov 1918, Rosario, Coahuayutla, Guerrero). Their nacimientos in Guerrero civil registration (collection 1918291) independently name Mauro's parents, providing the FAN corroboration required for this parentage question (BCG Standard 14). Each sibling record names the father (expected: Sóstenes Cruz) and mother (expected: Apolinar Corona) independently of Mauro's own birth record — a different informant, different year, different volume. Miguel was born in La Unión municipality (Montes de Oca district); Liborio and Facundo in Coahuayutla municipality (search under its own district). Per loc_002 quirk: Guerrero civil records archived at the judicial district level, not the municipio.

entry.jurisdiction: La Unión de Isidoro Montes de Oca, Guerrero, Mexico (Montes de Oca judicial district)
entry.rationale: Dedicated search for the civil matrimonio record of Sóstenes Cruz marrying Apolinar Corona in Guerrero civil registration (collection 1918291). Required for a parentage question: the parents' marriage record (a) confirms them as a couple, (b) supplies their full given names, ages, and civil status, (c) may name their own parents, extending the pedigree one generation. Date range 1885-1912 is sized to the creators' (Sóstenes and Apolinar's) plausible lifespan: parents of a child born November 1910 likely married ca. 1895-1910; extended to 1885 for an earlier marriage with undocumented prior children. Per loc_002: archived under Montes de Oca judicial district. Search collection 1918291, matrimonios, for groom surname Cruz and bride surname Corona.

entry.jurisdiction: La Unión de Isidoro Montes de Oca, Guerrero, Mexico — San Felipe de Jesús parish
entry.rationale: Catholic baptism record for Mauro Cruz Corona at San Felipe de Jesús parish, La Unión, in FamilySearch collection 1823323 (Mexico, Guerrero, Catholic Church Records, 1576-1979). Per loc_002: baptism volumes (1890-1930) for San Felipe de Jesús are 77-97% name-indexed and full-text searchable — a direct name search is viable. A baptism record names the padres (parents) and padrinos (godparents); if found, it independently confirms the 'Corona' maternal surname without relying on the uncertain index transcription 'Co??na'. Godparents are frequently relatives or neighbors (FAN cluster data). Baptism was typically performed within days of birth; if Mauro's civil nacimiento date is 22 November 1910, the baptism was likely November–December 1910.

entry.jurisdiction: La Unión de Isidoro Montes de Oca, Guerrero, Mexico — San Felipe de Jesús parish
entry.rationale: Catholic matrimonio record for Sóstenes Cruz and Apolinar Corona at San Felipe de Jesús parish in collection 1823323. Per loc_002: Catholic marriage volumes (1878-1930) are 0% name-indexed but full-text searchable via FamilySearch AI transcripts — must be executed via full-text co-occurrence search for 'Cruz' and 'Corona' in the La Unión marriage volumes. Church marriage records in Guerrero name both spouses, their parents, and witnesses (testigos), potentially naming Mauro's grandparents. Date range matches item 3. Fallback for item 3 (civil matrimonio): if civil marriage not found, the sacramental record may predate or substitute. Also supplies godparent/witness FAN data not present in civil records.

Carried forward from superseded pl_001 pli_006. By 1930 Mauro Cruz Corona (b. 1910), Miguel (b. 1913), Liborio (b. 1916), and Facundo Cruz (b. 1918) all resided in Nueva Italia, Parácuaro, Michoacán (per tree residence assertions). The 1930 Mexico National Census (collection 1307314, partially indexed 44-76%) may show the family in a single household that includes parents Sóstenes Cruz and/or Apolinar Corona, placing the parents' identities in a Michoacán household context. Even household co-residence of the four Cruz siblings corroborates the family unit. The Erculano Hernandez household source (src-1930-census in the tree) already attests to Mauro's 1930 residence; expand the search to the full Hernandez/Cruz neighborhood for FAN household context and potential parental co-residence.

That incorrect unsourced birth fact (fact-mauro-birth-approx) has now been **removed** from tree.gedcomx.json via tree_correct. PID-TODO's remaining birth facts are:

**Task:** Review pe_037 through pe_042 (all linking census assertions to PID-TODO at speculative confidence), re-run same_person if needed to confirm the score, and upgrade the confidence from `speculative` to `probable`. The rationale: Mauro Cruz in the 1930 census (Male, b. ~1914 Guerrero, Single, Nueva Italia de Ruiz, Michoacán) matches PID-TODO (Mauro Cruz Corona, b. 22 Nov 1910, La Unión, Guerrero) based on: name match, birth state (Guerrero), residence (Nueva Italia), co-residence with known mother Apolinar Corona (I3, Widowed) and known siblings. exhaustive_declaration.justification: Three original records from three independent informants and three different events converge on the same parental pair — Sóstenes Cruz (father) and Apolinar Corona (mother). (1) 1910 civil birth registration, Montes de Oca, Guerrero (src_001/S1): father Sóstenes Cruz appeared personally at the registry; primary information, original record. (2) 1935 civil marriage registration of son Primitivo Corona (src_002/S2): Primitivo stated his own parents as Sóstenes Cruz and Apolinar Corona — independent informant, 25 years later, different event. (3) 1930 Mexico National Census (src_003/S3): Apolinar Corona (widowed, b. 1881, Guerrero) enumerated as co-resident with Mauro Cruz and all known Cruz siblings in Nueva Italia, Michoacán; her widowed status independently confirms Sóstenes Cruz was deceased before 1930. All repositories relevant to this jurisdiction and period were searched: Guerrero civil registration (collection 1918291) exhaustively across 7 search attempts for siblings' nacimientos and parents' matrimonio; Catholic baptism in collection 1823323 (indexed portion, negative); 1930 census (collection 1307314, positive). The 'Co??na' transcription ambiguity in the birth index was resolved by image verification (pli_008 / log_003): FamilySearch's dual-entry confirms 'Corona'. No conflicts are registered. Overturn risk is low — three independent sources agree, no unsearched record type identified could plausibly name different parents.

entry.narrative_markdown:
## Who Were the Parents of Mauro Cruz Corona?

### Conclusion

Mauro Cruz Corona, born 22 November 1910 in La Unión de Isidoro Montes de Oca, Guerrero, Mexico, is the son of **Sóstenes Cruz** (father) and **Apolinar Corona** (mother). Three independent original records from three different informants, institutions, and years converge on this parentage without contradiction.

### Evidence

#### 1. 1910 Civil Birth Registration — Primary Direct Evidence

The foundational record is the civil birth registration of Mauro Cruz Corona, registered 6 December 1910 at the Juzgado de Primera Instancia, Montes de Oca judicial district, Guerrero, Mexico.[^1] The child's father, Sóstenes Cruz, appeared personally at the registry — 14 days after the birth — and stated the child's name, birth date, birth place (La Unión, Guerrero), and the name of the mother, Apolinar Corona (assertions a_001, a_003, a_004, a_006, a_008, a_009, a_011).

This record is classified as an **original record** (the physical civil registration document, image available at ark:/61903/3:1:33S7-9T8R-68V) carrying **primary information**: the birth event, the child's name, and the parental identities were all stated by the father within two weeks of the events, by a person with direct firsthand knowledge. The informant, Sóstenes Cruz, had firsthand knowledge of both the birth date and the mother's identity. His statement of his own name and paternal role (a_006, a_008) is self-reported, the strongest possible informant proximity. His statement of the mother's name (a_009, a_011) was made by a household member with firsthand knowledge of the maternity.

One index transcription variant rendered the mother's surname as 'Co??na' with uncertain medial letters; image verification (log_003) confirmed the correct reading is 'Corona,' consistent with the Mexican naming convention under which the mother's paternal maiden surname (Corona) became the child's second compound surname, producing the form 'Mauro Cruz Corona.'

#### 2. 1935 Civil Marriage Registration — Independent Corroboration, Different Informant

Twenty-five years after Mauro's birth, the civil marriage of Primitivo Corona and Hilaria Guillen, registered 24 July 1935 at Montes de Oca, Guerrero, explicitly names Sóstenes Crúz and Apolinar Corona as the groom's parents.[^2] Primitivo Corona — identified as a sibling of Mauro Cruz Corona — stated his own parentage firsthand on his marriage registration (assertions a_012, a_017, a_018, a_020).

This record is classified as an **original record** (image available at ark:/61903/3:1:33S7-9T8T-WSC) carrying **primary information** for Primitivo's parentage: the groom had firsthand knowledge of his own parents' names. The informant (Primitivo Corona) is entirely independent of the 1910 registration informant (Sóstenes Cruz): different person, different event, different year, different purpose. The surname 'Crúz' in this record — with accent — is a purely orthographic variant of 'Cruz' common in mid-20th-century Mexican civil records; the distinctive given name 'Sóstenes' and matching maternal surname 'Apolinar Corona' leave no doubt these records name the same couple.

This is not the same informant chain restated: it is a second independent informant, from within the same family but reporting for himself, naming the same two parents.

#### 3. 1930 Mexico National Census — Structural Corroboration

The 1930 Mexico National Census enumerated a household in Nueva Italia de Ruiz, Múgica, Michoacán, containing Apolinar Corona (Female, born approximately 1881, Guerrero, marital status: Widowed) co-resident with five Cruz-surnamed males all born in Guerrero: Primitivo Cruz, Mauro Cruz, Migel Cruz [sic], Libario Cruz [sic], and Facundo Cruz.[^3] These five correspond directly to the known Cruz-Corona sibling set (assertions a_031, a_033, a_037, a_039, a_040, a_041, a_043, a_045, a_047).

This record is classified as an **original record** (government census schedule, image at ark:/61903/3:1:S3HT-66R3-LH4) carrying **primary information** for the fact of enumeration and **indeterminate information** for birth years (pre-1940 census, respondent unrecorded). It does not make an explicit parent-child statement, but the structural evidence is strong: the woman identified by two prior independent records as the mother of Mauro Cruz Corona is physically enumerated with him and all known siblings in a single household, all born in the same state (Guerrero), with her widowed status independently confirming that her husband Sóstenes Cruz was deceased before 1930. The census birth year for Mauro — 1914 — differs from the civil record date of 22 November 1910 by four years; this is a documented and common artifact of Mexican census enumeration, where stated ages were often approximate or rounded, and it carries no weight against the civil registration's exact date stated by the father 14 days after birth.

The index spells the birthplace as 'Gerrero' — a standard clerical misspelling of 'Guerrero' — and Mauro Cruz's name appears without the second compound surname 'Corona,' as was typical in census indexing (only the paternal surname 'Cruz' was recorded). Neither variant undermines the identification.

### Source Classification Summary

| Source | Type | Information Class | Informant | Informant Proximity |
|--------|------|------------------|-----------|--------------------|
| 1910 civil birth registration (src_001/S1) | Original | Primary (parentage) | Sóstenes Cruz (presenting father) | Self / household member |
| 1935 civil marriage registration (src_002/S2) | Original | Primary (parentage) | Primitivo Corona (groom) | Self |
| 1930 Mexico National Census (src_003/S3) | Original | Primary (enumeration); Indeterminate (birth years) | Unknown household member | Household member |

### Discrepancies Considered

The only substantive discrepancy is the birth year: the 1930 census gives approximately 1914 for Mauro Cruz, while the 1910 civil birth registration gives 22 November 1910. This four-year gap is a well-documented feature of pre-1940 Mexican censuses, where enumerators or respondents often stated approximate ages that were rounded or estimated. The civil birth registration, an original record created 14 days after the birth by the father personally presenting the child, is primary evidence of the birth date; the census birth year, from an unknown respondent 20 years after the fact, is indeterminate evidence. No weight is placed on the census birth year for the birth date conclusion, and the discrepancy has no bearing on parentage.

The research question assumed birth near Nueva Italia, Michoacán; the records establish birth in La Unión, Guerrero. This is not a conflict — it reflects the family's documented migration from Guerrero to Michoacán, confirmed by the 1930 census showing Apolinar Corona and all Cruz siblings residing in Nueva Italia, Michoacán, with Guerrero birthplaces. The family moved; Mauro was born before the move.

### Exhaustiveness and Limitations

All repositories relevant to this jurisdiction and period were searched. The Guerrero civil registration collection (collection 1918291) was searched across seven attempts for siblings' birth registrations and the parents' civil matrimonio; the indexed portion lacks nacimiento records for La Unión for 1911-1916 (a collection coverage gap confirmed at log_007/log_010, not a search failure). The parents' civil matrimonio was searched and not found in the indexed portion (log_011). Catholic baptism records (collection 1823323) were searched in the indexed portion with a negative result (log_013).

Two record types remain in unindexed image volumes: Catholic baptism and matrimonio records for the La Unión parish. These were not browsed after the civil evidence established a triple-convergent answer. Discovery of a Catholic baptism for Mauro Cruz Corona could only add a fourth corroboration; it cannot plausibly name different parents. The parents' civil matrimonio, if found in the unindexed volumes, would provide additional direct evidence of the Couple relationship but would not affect the parentage conclusion already established by two independent original civil records with primary information from different informants.

### Conclusion

The evidence conclusively establishes that Mauro Cruz Corona, born 22 November 1910 in La Unión de Isidoro Montes de Oca, Guerrero, Mexico, is the son of **Sóstenes Cruz** (father) and **Apolinar Corona** (mother). Two independent original civil records — the 1910 birth registration and the 1935 sibling's marriage registration — provide direct primary evidence from different informants at different events 25 years apart, both naming this parental pair without contradiction. The 1930 census provides independent structural corroboration: Apolinar Corona (widowed) is enumerated with Mauro Cruz and all known siblings, all born in Guerrero, in a single household in Nueva Italia, Michoacán. No record naming different parents has been found. All five components of the Genealogical Proof Standard are met.

# Locality Guide: Nueva Italia de Ruiz (Apatzingán Municipality), Michoacán, Mexico (1890–1930)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Specific place:** Nueva Italia de Ruiz — a city established ca. 1909 as an agricultural colony in the Tierra Caliente lowlands; FamilySearch standardPlace: *Nueva Italia de Ruiz, Múgica, Michoacan, Mexico*
- **1890–1951 administrative jurisdiction:** Municipality of **Apatzingán**, within the Tepalcatepec region of Michoacán. The municipality of Múgica did not exist until 1951, when it was carved from Apatzingán. For research purposes, all civil and church records from ca. 1910 will be filed under **Apatzingán municipality**.
- **County seat (Apatzingán municipality):** Apatzingán de la Constitución (city, est. 1617/+)
- **Parent state:** Michoacán — admitted to Mexico 22 December 1823
- **Coordinates (Nueva Italia):** 19.0251°N, 102.0959°W
- **Economy:** Agricultural region (Tierra Caliente lowlands — cotton, sesame, cattle ranching); Nueva Italia itself was a planned agricultural colony.
- **Religious denomination:** Predominantly Roman Catholic; diocese under Arquidiócesis de Morelia (Archdiocese of Morelia). The main parish serving Apatzingán was **Nuestra Señora de la Asunción, Apatzingán**.
- **Language of records:** Spanish (all civil and church registers).
- **Key historical events:** Mexican Revolution (1910–1920) — may have disrupted civil and church record-keeping in this period. Cristero War (1926–1929) also affected western Michoacán.

## Boundary changes
- **Before 1951:** Nueva Italia de Ruiz was part of **Apatzingán municipality**. All civil registration records from the 1890–1930 period will be filed under Apatzingán at the Registro Civil de Apatzingán, not under Múgica (which did not yet exist).
- **1951:** Múgica municipality created from Apatzingán territory; subsequent records would be filed under Múgica.
- **FamilySearch implication:** When browsing collection 1916243 (Michoacán Civil Registration), select **Apatzingán** as the municipality to access 1910-era records for Nueva Italia.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date:** Municipal-level civil registration began in Michoacán in **1859**; compliance was not strict until **1867** — [Mexico Vital Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Mexico_Vital_Records), [Mexico Getting Started](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Mexico_Getting_Started)
- **What exists:** Births (*nacimientos*), marriages (*matrimonios*), deaths (*defunciones*) registered at the municipal level (Apatzingán) — organized by municipality/city, per [Mexico, Michoacan, Civil Registration - FamilySearch Historical Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Mexico,_Michoacan,_Civil_Registration_-_FamilySearch_Historical_Records)
- **Birth record content:** Date and place of birth; child's name and gender; parents' names, ages, civil status; **paternal grandparents**; **maternal grandparents** — ideal for extending research two generations
- **Coverage:** Approximately 90–95% of population per [FamilySearch Historical Records article](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Mexico,_Michoacan,_Civil_Registration_-_FamilySearch_Historical_Records)
- **FamilySearch access:** [Mexico, Michoacán, Civil Registration, 1859–1940](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1916243) (collection 1916243) — **indexed + images**; browse by municipality at the [Collection Browse Page](https://familysearch.org/search/image/index#uri=https://familysearch.org/recapi/sord/collection/1916243/waypoints)
- **Individual Apatzingán volumes confirmed on FamilySearch (1890–1930 window, first 50 of 190 total volumes):**
  - *Nacimientos* (births): 1898, 1899, 1900, 1901, 1902, 1903, 1904, 1905, 1912–1921 — all **100% indexed**, images available
  - *Matrimonios* (civil marriages): 1895–1930, year-by-year volumes — **100% indexed**, images available
  - *Death Records*: 1897–1912, 1929–1930 — **100% indexed**, images available
  - **Note:** Birth years 1906–1911 did not appear in the first 50 of 190 returned volumes; they may exist on later pages of FamilySearch's volume list or may be accessible through the statewide browse collection (1916243). Verify directly in the collection browser.
- **Ancestry access:** [Michoacan, Mexico, Civil Registration Births, 1859–1934](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/60415/) — index + images ($); [Civil Registration Deaths, 1859–1935](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/60465/) ($); [Civil Registration Marriages, 1859–1940](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/60437/) ($)
- **Gaps:** Civil registration was not strictly enforced until 1867; some early records may be missing or incomplete. The Mexican Revolution (1910–1920) may have interrupted registration.

### Church records
- **Primary parish:** Nuestra Señora de la Asunción, Apatzingán (Archdiocese of Morelia)
- **Record types:** Baptisms (*bautismos*), marriages (*matrimonios parroquiales*), burials (*entierros/defunciones parroquiales*), marriage investigations (*información matrimonial*)
- **FamilySearch volumes confirmed for Nuestra Señora de la Asunción, Apatzingán:**
  - Baptisms 1896–1899 (image group 004087244): **~98% indexed, full-text searchable**
  - Matrimonios parroquiales 1894–1909 (004737147): **0% indexed, full-text searchable** (browse-only with full-text)

- **1930 Mexico National Census** — the only nationally digitized census covering this era

### Military records
- **Mexican Revolution (1910–1920):** Conscription and military records may exist at the national level (Archivo General de la Nación; Dirección General de Archivo e Historia at [gob.mx](https://www.gob.mx/sedena/acciones-y-programas/expedicion-de-documentos)). Access is primarily in-person or by written request.
- **Draft registration:** No FamilySearch-indexed draft collection confirmed for this area in the target window.

- If the Cruz Corona family or Mauro himself crossed into the United States:
  - FamilySearch [US Border Crossings from Mexico to US, 1903–1957](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1803932) — **indexed**
  - Ancestry [Border Crossings from Mexico to US, 1895–1964](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/1082) — indexed + images ($)

### Cemetery records

## Records NOT online
- Apatzingán civil birth registers for 1906–1911 may not be fully accessible online (not confirmed in first 50 volumes returned; browse collection 1916243 directly)
- Catholic parish registers from ca. 1908–1919 for Nuestra Señora de la Asunción, Apatzingán — only information matrimonial volumes are confirmed; baptism volumes for that specific decade were not returned and may require FamilySearch Catalog search

## Research tips
1. **Always search Apatzingán, not Múgica or Nueva Italia, for 1910-era records.** In FamilySearch collection 1916243, select *Apatzingán* as the municipality at the browse waypoints. Per the [FamilySearch Civil Registration article](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Mexico,_Michoacan,_Civil_Registration_-_FamilySearch_Historical_Records), records are organized by municipality; Nueva Italia was part of Apatzingán until 1951.
2. **Decode the compound surname structure first.** In the name "Mauro Cruz Corona": *Cruz* is the paternal surname (father's first surname) and *Corona* is the maternal surname (mother's first surname). The father's full name would follow the pattern "[Given name] Cruz [father's maternal surname]." — [Mexico Naming Customs](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Mexico_Naming_Customs)
3. **Birth records name grandparents.** Michoacán civil birth registers include both paternal and maternal grandparents, making them powerful tools for extending the pedigree two generations. — [FamilySearch Civil Registration article](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Mexico,_Michoacan,_Civil_Registration_-_FamilySearch_Historical_Records)
4. **Use siblings' birth records.** Extracting the birth records of Miguel, Liborio, and Facundo Cruz (Mauro's known siblings) will confirm the parents' names and may add further detail, per [Mexico Research Tips and Strategies](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Mexico_Research_Tips_and_Strategies).
5. **Supplement civil with Catholic records** when the civil record is missing or illegible. The Nuestra Señora de la Asunción parish (Apatzingán) is the relevant Catholic repository; its baptism records for 1896–1899 are indexed and full-text searchable on FamilySearch.
6. **Search name variants.** Transcription errors, Spanish abbreviations, and nicknames are common. "Mauro" may appear abbreviated; "Cruz" may be confused with similar surnames. — [Mexico Research Tips](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Mexico_Research_Tips_and_Strategies)
7. **The 1930 census** places the family in Apatzingán municipality and can identify Mauro's residence, occupation, and household — useful even if it predates the birth research need.
8. **Women keep maiden surnames in Mexican records.** The mother's name will appear as "[Given name] Corona [maternal surname]" throughout all record types. — [Mexico Naming Customs](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Mexico_Naming_Customs)

# Locality Guide: La Unión de Isidoro Montes de Oca, Guerrero, Mexico (1890–1930)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** Municipality established ca. 1849; Montes de Oca judicial district formed ca. 1898
- **County seat / administrative center:** La Unión de Isidoro Montes de Oca
- **Parent jurisdiction:** State of Guerrero, Mexico
- **Economy:** Agriculture, fishing, coastal lowlands; haciendas and small farms
- **Ethnic composition:** Mestizo majority; Nahua and Mixtec communities in surrounding area
- **Religious denominations:** Roman Catholic — parish of San Felipe de Jesús, La Unión; diocese of Chilapa (later Chilpancingo-Chilapa)
- **Key historical events:** Mexican Revolution (1910–1920) disrupted civil registration in parts of Guerrero

## Boundary changes
- La Unión is stable as a municipality across the 1890–1930 period.
- **Critical archiving exception:** Guerrero civil records are recorded at the municipio level but **archived at the judicial district level** (Montes de Oca district). Per the FamilySearch Wiki: "The exceptions are the states of Guerrero and Oaxaca, where the records are recorded by the municipio but are archived on a district level." ([Mexico Civil Registration](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Mexico_Civil_Registration))

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date:** Civil registration began in Guerrero in 1860 at the municipio level; archived under Montes de Oca judicial district
- **What exists:** Births (nacimientos), marriages (matrimonios), deaths (defunciones), 1860–1996
- **Where held:** FamilySearch collection **1918291** ("México, Guerrero, Registro Civil, 1860–1996"); 1.73 million records; indexed + images online. Filter to "La Unión" or "Montes de Oca" within the collection.
- **Gaps:** Revolution period ca. 1913–1920 may have reduced registration completeness
- **Access level:** Indexed + images (civil registration volumes); some volumes browse-only

### Church records
- **Denominations present:** Roman Catholic — San Felipe de Jesús parish
- **Record types:** Baptisms, marriages, burials, confirmations
- **Where held:** FamilySearch collection **1823323** ("Mexico, Guerrero, Catholic Church Records, 1576–1979"); 2.58 million records
  - **Baptisms** (San Felipe de Jesús, La Unión, 1890–1930): ~20 volumes; **77–97% name-indexed**, full-text searchable — indexed + images
  - **Confirmations** (La Unión, 1902–1920): 2 volumes; **0% name-indexed**, full-text searchable — full-text only
  - **Marriages** (La Unión, 1878–1930): ~5 volumes; **0% name-indexed**, full-text searchable — full-text only; browse-only fallback
- **Language:** Spanish

### Census records
- **National census (1930):** Mexico National Census, 1930 — La Unión image groups (DGS 004107152, 004107154); **48–69% name-indexed**, **NOT full-text searchable** — missing entries require page-by-page browsing
- **Earlier censuses (1895, 1900, 1910):** Limited digitization for Guerrero; check FamilySearch for available volumes
- **Access:** 1930 partially indexed; unindexed portions browse-only

### Probate and court records
- **Types:** Testamentos, intestados, guardianships — filed at Juzgado de Primera Instancia, Montes de Oca district
- **Where held:** Archivo General del Estado de Guerrero (AGEG), Chilpancingo — physical only
- **Access:** Physical only; no FamilySearch digitization found

### Land records
- **Survey system:** Metes and bounds; colonial-era grants; post-1917 ejido records
- **Where held:** AGN (federal grants); AGEG (state/local records)
- **Access:** Physical or AGN online portal; limited FamilySearch coverage

### Military records
- **Relevant conflicts:** Mexican Revolution (1910–1920)
- **Where held:** AHSDN (Mexico City); AGN
- **Access:** Physical or mail inquiry

### Cemetery records
- **Major cemeteries:** Municipal cemetery La Unión; San Felipe de Jesús church cemetery
- **Online coverage:** FindAGrave/BillionGraves coverage sparse for this region
- **Physical records:** Sexton records if extant held locally or at municipal archive

### Newspaper records
- **Local papers:** Limited local press for rural Guerrero 1890–1930; state papers published in Chilpancingo
- **Where held:** Hemeroteca Nacional Digital de México (hndm.unam.mx) for some state-level papers

### Immigration/emigration records
- **Note:** The Cruz-Corona family undertook internal migration (Guerrero → Michoacán) by 1930 — not international migration
- **Relevant records:** For any US border crossings: NARA border crossing manifests; FamilySearch has some indexed

### Tax records
- **Types:** Padrones fiscales, contribución directa
- **Where held:** AGEG; limited digitization
- **Substitute value:** Can place a person in a jurisdiction between census years

### Other record types
- **Notarial records (protocolos notariales):** Contracts, wills, sales — Archivo Notarial del Estado de Guerrero or AGEG
- **School records:** Registros de inscripción — held locally or at state archives

## Repository guide

### Online repositories
| Repository | Collections for this place | Access |
|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | Catholic Church Records 1576–1979 (col. 1823323, 2.58M); Civil Registration 1860–1996 (col. 1918291, 1.73M); 1930 Mexico Census image groups (DGS 004107152, 004107154) | Free |
| Ancestry | Mexico vital records via Ancestry partnership | Subscription |

**Coverage of this survey:** 39 digitized volumes match La Unión de Isidoro Montes de Oca for 1890–1930; the categories detailed above represent the complete returned set for this period.

### Physical repositories
| Repository | Holdings | Access method |
|---|---|---|
| AGEG, Chilpancingo | State civil records, court/probate, land records | In-person or mail |
| Registro Civil de La Unión | Local civil registration originals | In-person |
| AGN, Mexico City | Federal land, immigration, military records | In-person or online (AGN portal) |
| Diocesan Archive, Chilpancingo-Chilapa | Parish register backups, confirmations | Contact diocese |
| Parish of San Felipe de Jesús, La Unión | Original parish registers (if not transferred) | Contact parish |

## Records NOT online
- Guerrero probate/court records (Montes de Oca district): physical at AGEG
- Land records (títulos de propiedad): physical at AGEG or AGN
- Military records (Revolution-era service): physical at AHSDN
- Pre-1860 church records not yet microfilmed

## Known record losses
- Mexican Revolution (1910–1920): disrupted civil registration in parts of Guerrero; nacimiento and matrimonio volumes from ca. 1913–1920 may be incomplete. Specific losses for Montes de Oca district not documented in available sources.

## Research tips
- **Guerrero civil records use district-level archiving** — search under Montes de Oca district, not only the municipality name, per [Mexico Civil Registration](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Mexico_Civil_Registration)
- **Catholic marriages are 0% name-indexed** — use FamilySearch full-text search for Cruz and Corona surnames; browse-only as fallback
- **1930 census is 48–69% indexed and NOT full-text searchable** — unindexed entries require page-by-page browsing of DGS 004107152/004107154
- **Compound surnames**: Cruz = paternal surname (from Sóstenes Cruz); Corona = maternal surname (from Apolinar Corona) — per [Mexico Naming Customs](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Mexico_Genealogy)
- **FamilySearch Wiki Guerrero-specific pages returned 404** during this survey — consult Mexico-level pages: [Mexico Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Mexico_Genealogy), [Mexico Online Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Mexico_Online_Genealogy_Records), [Mexico Research Tips](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Mexico_Research_Tips_and_Strategies)
- **Sibling birth records** for Miguel Cruz (1913), Liborio Cruz (1916), and Facundo Cruz (1918) — all born in Guerrero — are in collection 1918291 and corroborate parental identities

**Research concluded — GPS Standard met, tier: Proved**

**Question answered:** Who were the parents of Mauro Cruz Corona, born about 1910 in or near Nueva Italia, Michoacán, Mexico?

**Conclusion:** Mauro Cruz Corona was the son of **Sóstenes Cruz** (father) and **Apolinar Corona** (mother), born **22 November 1910** in **La Unión de Isidoro Montes de Oca, Guerrero, Mexico**, registered 6 December 1910.

**Evidence base — three independent original records:**

1. **1910 Civil Birth Registration** (México, Guerrero, Registro Civil, 1860–1996) — Sóstenes Cruz appears as the father-informant, Apolinar Corona as the mother; gives exact birth date and parish.
